# BigQuery's mathematical function documentation specifies FLOAT64 for every CBRT input.
# Source: third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/mathematical_functions.md
# UNNEST also checks runtime inputs rather than only analyzer-folded literals.

SELECT TYPEOF(CBRT(x)) FROM UNNEST([8]) x
=> "FLOAT64"

SELECT TYPEOF(CBRT(x)) FROM UNNEST([NUMERIC '8']) x
=> "FLOAT64"

SELECT TYPEOF(CBRT(x)) FROM UNNEST([BIGNUMERIC '8']) x
=> "FLOAT64"

SELECT TYPEOF(CBRT(x)) FROM UNNEST([8.0]) x
=> "FLOAT64"

# Round the documented example to avoid depending on floating-point rounding and JSON spelling.
SELECT CAST(CBRT(x) AS INT64) FROM UNNEST([NUMERIC '27']) x
=> "3"

SELECT CAST(CBRT(x) AS INT64) FROM UNNEST([BIGNUMERIC '27']) x
=> "3"

SELECT CBRT(x) FROM UNNEST([CAST(NULL AS NUMERIC)]) x
=> null

SELECT SAFE.CBRT(x) FROM UNNEST([CAST(NULL AS BIGNUMERIC)]) x
=> null

SELECT CAST(CBRT(x) AS INT64) FROM UNNEST([NUMERIC '0']) x
=> "0"

SELECT CAST(SAFE.CBRT(x) AS INT64) FROM UNNEST([BIGNUMERIC '0']) x
=> "0"
